 Flash flooding along Ocoee River forces evacuations as river reaches record high levels
 Staff Photo by Seth Carpenter/ A mound of debris is caught on the William T. ‘Boss’ Mull Memorial Bridge in McCaysville, Ga. following a flood on the Ocoee and Toccoa Rivers on Thursday, Nov. 5, 2026. Staff photo by Jay Luzardo / Water floods the Big Creek access point on the Ocoee River in Polk County on Thursday. 
 By Jay Luzardo 
 November 5, 2026 
 11 min read 
 Flash flooding along the Ocoee River forced residents in southeastern Polk County and parts of North Georgia to search for higher ground early Thursday morning.
 The river reached its highest level ever recorded, cresting at just over 18 feet after the rainfall Thursday morning, according to the National Weather Service office in Morristown. The previous record was 17.75 feet, set in 1990.
 Some areas, including Gilmer and Fannin counties in Georgia, saw more than 10 inches of rain fall over several hours overnight, officials said, which triggered the flooding on the Ocoee. Polk County, Tennessee, saw around three inches, according to the NWS, and rescue operations there began around 1 a.m. Thursday.
 (READ MORE: Copperhill, Tenn., and McCaysville, Ga., slammed by floods )
 As of Thursday afternoon, when crews finished combing the area, 68 people had been rescued, officials said.
